title: Process simplification and cost: affected-test gates, converging reviews, honest prices
description: Merges the handoff's phase 2 (process simplification, sketch section 0) and phase 4 (cost: F597 and F577 first, then research N1-N5, then sketch section 3 incl. 3a) into one phase so it is reviewed once. Order inside the phase follows the handoff: the meter's dedup (F597) lands before any task that produces or prints a cost figure, because every figure after it would otherwise be biased in the plugin's favour; the price table (F577/N1) lands before Haiku-first review (N2) and the CI cost gate, because Haiku 5.5 is priced at `_default` today. Process items: affected-test gates per task with the full gate once per phase (F596, incl. its e2e extension), derived follower scope, review convergence (F605), one-command release. Cost items: one price table with effective dates and record-time stamping (3a), the CLI's costUSD beside the plugin's reading, the reviewer's diff computed once (N5), Haiku-first review behind a config key (N2), the git-snapshot report (N4), maxTurns caps (N12), cache-friendly dispatch prompts and briefs, an enforced one-line hand-back (F567), a CI cost regression gate over recorded sessions, and a design-and-measurement task only for running the phase cycle as a plugin Workflow (N3, implementation needs a paid probe). F575 is not included: it was addressed by P119.7 and P121.12. Prices were verified against Anthropic's pricing and models pages on 2026-10-10 (quoted in openChoices). No task makes a paid model call. Open choices settled by the orchestrator under the user's overnight mandate (2026-10-10), each the structurally correct option: one price table living in hooks/_config.py with _usage_core deriving it; no shipped _default row (a project-declared one is still honoured); effectiveFrom = the date the plugin first read the rate, older rows labelled; ship the published rate and show the CLI reading beside it, calling neither the bill; a carried low goes to a pending task in one plan-level carry-forward phase; Haiku-first review off by default behind review.cascade; e2e selection = runner related list + changed list + meta.coupling, else every spec with the reason printed; followers for user projects from meta.followers.command plus F599 companions; hand-backs enforced by a SubagentStop hook after a payload probe; the CI cost gate reads redacted committed recordings; maxTurns = 2x the largest measured request count with the command beside it; F575 closed in the register after one timed run.
desiredOutcome: A task gate runs what the change can break, sign-off converges in at most the configured rounds, and every cost figure is priced at the rate in effect when it was recorded.

Keep the ring's bound and drop the counts of an id that leaves it. Correct the module docstring's premise to what was measured (the block repeats, except subagent output_tokens, which grows) and the README's 'One trap' paragraph to match. tasks.title: Sign-off converges: re-review only for med+ or red fixes, lows carried, rounds capped
tasks.description: F605. In drive-phase's triage: (1) a re-review is owed only for a fix task whose finding was med or high, or whose gate went red; a fixed low closes on its own green gate and fixes_after()/owed_tasks() stop listing it. (2) The triage's recommended answer for a low finding is carry (status `carried`, carriedTo a parked task - see openChoices for the target), and render_triage prints that as the default; fix stays available. (3) A re-review reads only the fix tasks' diffs (phase-diff-in-brief) and its brief says a new low in a fix is carried, not looped. (4) A round cap per phase, config review.maxRounds (default 2): reaching it prints the findings still open, the rounds' cost so far read from the usage ledger by phase (with its pricing basis, or 'unpriced' where it is), and asks once (carry all / one more round / sign-off with accept-open). The cap and the counts live in the driver's state, so a lost state file re-derives the round count from the filed phase returns rather than resetting to zero. Add the config key to hooks/_config.py DEFAULTS, _config_rules, the schema and the README config table. Red first: a review returning one med and two lows dispatches one fix task and one re-review over that fix's diff, the two lows end carried, and no third review is dispatched. Also measured in P123's review rounds: a fix task made from a finding defaults to tdd even when the finding is a missing test or a pin over a fix that already landed (P123.63, P123.66), so the red-first helper rightly refuses it and the task must be cancelled and re-added as regression - choose the fix task's mode from the finding: a finding whose resolution only adds a case over code already at HEAD is regression, with the red shown by restoring the old code in a scratch copy.

tasks.title: Phase review can run Haiku-first and escalate on a computed predicate, off by default
tasks.description: N2. Config review.cascade: 'off' (default) | 'haiku-first'. When on, dispatch_phase_review dispatches the reviewer with model=claude-haiku-5-5 and the same brief and JSON return; a pure predicate escalate(filed, phase) decides whether a second, Sonnet dispatch is owed: any finding, any cannot-tell or missing intent input, any recorded open choice, red-first not proved, or an existing test file modified (the signals signals_fired() and the brief already compute). The second filing supersedes the first in _filed_returns, and both are kept in evidence with their model. The predicate's verdict per phase is computed offline over the recorded phase fixtures and printed by a selftest; the cascade's false-negative rate needs model calls and is not measured here (openChoices), which is why the default is off. Depends on the price table so a Haiku dispatch is priced, not _default. Evidence (research report 2026-10-12, probe 2): Haiku matched Opus on the target defect at about 1/18 of the cost ONLY under the clause-quoting rule of intent-against-task-text; one scenario, false-positive rate not measured - so this depends on that task and its predicate must be re-measured before default-on.

tasks.title: A task gate also runs every test its change can break; the full gate runs once per phase

tasks.title: tools/release.py cuts a release end to end, stopping on the first red and resuming
tasks.description: Sketch section 0. Steps, each recorded in a resumable state file and skipped on resume once done: preflight (the open-bug and provisional-phase question guard-release asks, read from its own predicate, plus verify.sh --release's preflight); bump plugin.json; finalize the CHANGELOG section; the followers in verify.sh's #R order (README curl pins, examples/report.sh incl. docs/index.html, the scale demo commands check-rendered-artifacts --how prints, screenshots); tools/verify.sh --release; the release commit; push to a ci/<version> branch and gh workflow run ci.yml --ref it; wait for that run on that exact SHA (a cancelled run is not a failed one - read conclusion); annotated tag; push main and the tag; gh release create with the CHANGELOG section; check-release-published. The first red stops with the step, its excerpt and the resume command. Every remote step is named before it runs and nothing is pushed without an explicit --push the user typed (CLAUDE.md: permission to commit is not permission to push). guard-release learns to treat an invocation of tools/release.py as a publishing command so the #release-with-bugs bypass still governs it. The ci step is callable alone (release.py ci <ref>) so a landed phase can run CI the same way. A selftest drives every step against a fake runner, including resume after a stop at each step.

tasks.title: Doctor reports the git-snapshot setting and the README cost section names it
tasks.description: N4. A plugin cannot set includeGitInstructions or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS for its users (its settings carry only agent and subagentStatusLine), so this is a report and a documented recommendation. /audit:doctor reads the effective value (env var, then project .claude/settings.local.json and settings.json, then user settings) and names where it came from; it also reads, from the session's subagent transcripts, each later dispatch's first-request cache read and write so the user sees whether starts are served from cache. The README's cost section names the setting, recommends it at project level (a user-level setting removes Claude's built-in git instructions from every session), and states that the plugin's executors never commit and the driver commits by script. No figure is printed without the reading that produced it.

tasks.title: An executor or reviewer reply longer than its filed line is sent back once
tasks.description: F567: 'hand back the line above as your whole reply' is printed by submit and followed by no executor (measured hand-backs ran to kilobytes). A new SubagentStop hook, scoped by agent_type to the plugin's executor and reviewer: submit writes the line it printed to the state dir keyed by the task id the agent's meta description starts with; the hook compares last_assistant_message to that line and, when the reply is longer, returns decision block once with the line as the reason, so the agent's final message - the one the main loop carries - becomes that line. tasks.title: The phase cycle as a plugin Workflow has a design and an offline measurement
tasks.description: N3, design and measurement only - no implementation, because the decisive facts (hooks firing inside workflow-spawned agents, the stagger's cache read, the main loop's real saving) need a paid probe. Write the design: run-phase.js's stages, the Haiku runner that calls drive-phase next and returns {exit, print} by schema, the on-disk token the script must re-read so a mis-relayed print cannot mis-route the loop, how every decide ends the run (workflows take no mid-run input), the fallback to today's Agent path for orgs with workflows off, the Claude Code version floor for COMPATIBILITY.md, and the guarantees to re-argue (gate independence, plan gate inside workflow agents, nothing owed to a human lands unseen). Measure offline with tools/stream-cost.py on recorded sessions: the main loop's spend between dispatches and the hand-back rows, each figure beside the command that produced it. End with the paid probe's exact protocol and the readings that would accept or reject the design.

tasks.title: A phase boundary is a context boundary: a chained run starts each phase fresh and status shows the carried context

(1) When the drive prints `done` and the phase command continues to a next phase, the command body (commands/phase.md and the run/drive reference) directs a fresh context per phase: clear and re-enter with `/audit:phase <next>`, stated as the step, not a tip. Micro-test: two trivial phases driven back to back as the command directs; the second phase's first orchestrator request carries no more context than a fresh entry within a stated margin (an offline fixture over recorded transcript rows, no paid call). tasks.title: The intent check grades the diff against the task text, and the drive checks tests.add against the filed tests
tasks.description: F633, measured on the testbed with a plain-session baseline and a blind A/B review: P5.3's text said src is set when the card ENTERS the viewport; the executor shipped `rootMargin: "200px 0px"`, said so, and renamed its test to 'once the card is near the viewport'; the phase reviewer's intentCheck answered `matches` on the basis of the executor's restatement. The blind pass also found two med defects the phase review missed. (1) The intent check QUOTES THE TASK TEXT and compares the diff and the tests against it - never against the outcome text or the test titles; a restatement whose scope differs from the task text is itself a finding, quoting both. (2) The reviewer brief puts the task text first and the executor's return last, labelled as the claim under review. (3) The drive diffs `tests.add` against the test names the return files, mechanically, and a declared case with no filed counterpart is a finding before any reviewer runs. Red-first: a fixture where the task says 'enters' and the return says 'near' with a 200px margin must answer `diverges` and quote both; a declared tests.add case missing from the return is named by the drive. (4) Measured on the testbed with the SAME model (plain Sonnet vs the plugin's Sonnet executors, blind A/B): the plugin's version alone shipped a lazy-load test that cannot fail, an e2e that drives the real server action (a key in env sends real mail), and a test-readiness race (asserting enabled state the SSR HTML already has). So the reviewer brief also asks, per declared test: can it fail on the unfixed code (the red-first block, or say it was never seen red), and does any test reach a real external service or side effect (mail, payment, network) rather than a stub - each a finding with its file:line. Faults: F633. (5) A FALSIFIER PER TEST, run by the drive at near-zero model cost (about +0.005 USD per task, research report 2026-10-12-agent-output-quality-research.md): every planned test carries a line 'must fail if <small code change>'; after the executor files, the drive applies that patch in a temporary tree (never the executor's tree) and runs the test, and a test that survives is a finding with file:line. A patch that breaks the build is could-not-run, never a kill. This REPLACES a revert-to-base check, which probe 1 measured as too weak: the plugin's P5.3 test fails on the revert yet survives the 'src set on mount' mutant, the real defect class; the plain Sonnet test kills both mount and margin_200 (artefacts danuvia-baseline/research-p53-plugin/probe-artifacts/probe1/*.log). (6) Parity in interaction states: when a task's design source names `:focus`/`:hover` rules for a form or control (as flux.css `.field input:focus` did), task synthesis writes into tests.add a design-parity case that snapshots that control's own box in its focus state (and hover where defined), not only rest, as a clipped element snapshot of that control or a computed-style assertion - a 1% threshold over a whole section hid a 2px ring (about 0.2% of the section) (2px/4px against the design's 9px, found by a live getComputedStyle probe). (7) Executor brief: scope must never push an executor into an inferior design. P6.3's plugin executor faked a 'Resend mock' by rewriting the browser response because `playwright.config.ts` was outside its scope; the plain session edited the config and ran a real mock. When the right design needs file X outside `files`, the executor files a widening request naming X and why, and does not work around it; P124's companions do not cover test infrastructure. Source: testbed monitor, 2026-10-12, at the owner's request. (8) Probe 2 (24 reviewer runs, Opus/Sonnet/Haiku, real P5.3 brief section): the brief as filed, task text first with the claim labelled, and the claim hidden each found 0/3 `diverges`; ONLY a CLAUSE-QUOTING RULE worked, 3/3 on all three models - the reviewer quotes each task clause, judges the diff against it, and a scope difference is `diverges`. So (1)-(2) are implemented as that rule, and: a contradicted clause carries a MED severity floor (4 of 6 Opus/Sonnet runs rated it low, which review-convergence would park as a carried low); the intent answer splits 'does the diff do what was asked' from 'does the claim describe the diff'; the phase brief carries tests.add, which it lacks today. (9) The tests.add-vs-filed-tests check of (3) cannot be a string diff: as one it flags 72 of 77 danuvia tasks, mostly Serbian plan text against English test titles. It matches a declared case by a verbatim title the executor must reuse, or by a clause mapping the return files; never a fuzzy string compare.

tasks.title: A task's model follows its recorded complexity as well as its risk, with the reason shown before approval
tasks.description: F634 (owner-raised, measured on the testbed): `audit-task._model_floor` routes opus only for `risk: high`, and risk is blast radius, not difficulty - nearly every testbed task ran on Sonnet, including the plan's hardest code (an astronomy core, a WebGL sky layer), because each was low risk; no planning step asks about difficulty. (1) A task records `complexity` (low/med/high) with a one-line basis, separate from risk, written by planning (init synthesis, `/audit:phase add`, `audit-task add`/`scope`) and validated by the manifest schema and rules (additive: a plan without it stays valid and reads as unrecorded, never defaulted). (2) Routing: opus when risk is high OR complexity is high, else sonnet; the caller's explicit `--model` still wins; a config key (`executor.modelByComplexity`, documented in COMPATIBILITY.md as added) can turn the complexity arm off. (3) The plan preview and `/audit:status` show each task's model and the reason it was chosen (risk, complexity, or the caller). (4) Escalation: after a retry, or a med+ finding on a Sonnet attempt, the next attempt of that task runs on opus, journaled with the reason. Red-first: two low-risk fixture tasks - a WebGL scene marked complexity high and a copy edit marked low - route to opus and sonnet; a retried Sonnet task's next dispatch names opus and the journal row says why. Faults: F634.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: a low-risk task with complexity high routes to opus and one with complexity low to sonnet; an explicit --model wins; a plan without complexity stays valid and reads as unrecorded

tasks.title: Parallel waves respect a shared external-resource budget: resources in config, needs on a task, and status says why a task was held

Add `resources: {name: capacity}` to audit.config.json (schema + config rules, additive, documented in COMPATIBILITY.md), `needs: [name]` on a task (plan schema + rules, additive), cap wave membership where waves are computed so a wave never holds more tasks needing a resource than its capacity, and have status/the drive say which task was held and for which resource. In the scheduler, not in executor prose. Red-first: two ready tasks both needing `port3100` with capacity 1 never share a wave, the held one is named with the resource; without `resources` the waves are unchanged. Faults: F508.

tasks.title: No report table can widen the page at any width, by construction rather than by font margin
tasks.description: Carried from P126-R2 (med, P126 phase review 2026-10-13). P126.1 made the hostile-content leg green on CI by letting the bugs table's test-gate pills wrap (`white-space:normal`), which lowers that column's narrowest width - so the page passes by margin at CI's fonts (reproduced with DejaVu in mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.56.0-jammy: +31px before, 0 after), not by an invariant: any table whose columns' min-content widths sum past the column can still widen the document above the breakpoint where `.tablewrap` starts to scroll. The structural options trade against the sticky header: (a) `.tablewrap{overflow-x:auto}` at every width - a contained scroll that can never widen the document, but `position:sticky` on thead then sticks to the wrapper, not the viewport; (b) keep the viewport-sticky header and give every non-prose column a bounded min-width plus `<wbr>` in every renderer-emitted unbroken run; (c) a JS-measured fallback that switches a table to (a) only when it overflows. Decide with the owner, implement, and add a hostile-leg case that plants a token in EVERY column kind at the narrowest unframed width on a wide-font fixture so the margin cannot be what passes it. Not a 3.2.0 regression: CI's hostile leg is green on 3.3.0.

add: tools/check-report-interactive.mjs: a token planted in every column kind of every table, at the narrowest unframed width with a wide fallback font, widens nothing

tasks.title: The PII check and the write scrub answer 'is this a home path' with one predicate
tasks.description: Recurring class observed 2026-10-13 in P126: a reviewer's prose phrase made of words joined by slashes was flagged by tools/check-committed-pii.py's posix-home detector in the finding row, the fix task's description, the reviewer return, the next executor's return and the plan's copy of its outcome - each time a new BASELINE row, five in one phase, and four earlier rows in BASELINE for the same shape. The write scrub (_machine_paths) fires posix-home only when a separator stands before the home word; the committed-artifact check fires on `home/` at any token start 'by design'. Two readers disagree on what a home path is, so honest prose costs a baseline row per copy and every copy is a gate going red. Decide the one predicate (with its measurement over this tree's committed artifacts and the detector's purpose: catching a home directory whose leading separator was cut), make both readers call it, retire the BASELINE rows it makes dead, and pin both directions (a cut home path still found; prose with slashes not).
